Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\parallel-session-worktree-isolation.md:136:- **Topic-named verdict file write-collision (operator-discipline anti-pattern)** — `.claude/state/codex_consult_<topic>_OUT.txt` files write-collide if two parallel worktrees fire T1 on the same topic; second writer wins, silently overwriting the first. Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\synthesis-layer-verify.md:62:**Why HNF matters**: it's the highest-value report shape but easiest to mistake for "agent failed to ship." An agent that probes the brief's assumption and finds it wrong has saved a wrong-direction ship — that's a SUCCESS at the discipline layer, not a failure. The synthesis-layer recovery is to update the brief / drop the patch / redirect to the correct target — never to re-spawn under the same (now-refuted) assumption.
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\synthesis-layer-verify.md:64:**HNF as cite-vs-concept sibling**: HNF reports are often the empirical refutation of a brief-level cite-vs-concept failure. Brief asserts X exists at file:line; agent probes; X doesn't exist. Brief's assumption was a CONCEPT (loose familiarity) not a CITE (verified file:line). HNF surfaces this gap. (Cite-vs-concept semantic-equivalence remains FORWARD-REF in claude-sota; the parent CCC narrative is TIER-3 provenance only until ported with TIER-1/TIER-2 backing.)
Z:\claude-sota\.claude\rules\synthesis-layer-verify.md:83:**Distinguishes from §Reporting categories above**: §Reporting categories classifies REPORT shape (OVER/UNDER/HNF — about agent's output). §Subclaim-type discriminator classifies SOURCE shape (UPSTREAM/OPERATIONAL/CATEGORY — about what's being verified). Orthogonal axes — a UPSTREAM-CLAIM probe may produce HNF, OVER, or UNDER report.

docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:10:    ### CR-12 disposition lattice (5 classes — Wave 134 Fire 27 series codification)
docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:12:    Beyond the **install-source priority order** (PRIMARY/SECONDARY/TERTIARY) above, every upstream-vs-incumbent relationship falls into ONE of 5 classes. Wave 134 Fire 27 series empirically mapped all 5:
docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:18:    3. **PARTIAL-OVERLAP** — incumbent and candidate cover overlapping function via DIFFERENT MECHANISMS. Disposition: **CASE-BY-CASE**, typically CITE-PATTERN-ONLY or STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT. Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-C mem0 (fact-extraction-based memory) vs eee graphiti (temporal-KG-based) vs mcp-memory (sqlite-vec-based) — same memory layer, different mechanisms. Codex T1 verdict at `.claude/state/codex_consult_w134_f27c_mem0_OUT.txt` STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT conf=0.87.
docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:20:    4. **PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT** — parallel API surfaces but different scopes; both can coexist. Disposition: **INSTALL as ALTERNATIVE (not PRIMARY)** — primary incumbent retains canonical position. Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-A openai-agents-python (vs Anthropic `claude-agent-sdk-python` @ HEAD `b512f256`) — Anthropic SDK = direct CC control plane (PRIMARY); OpenAI SDK = provider-agnostic orchestration (ALTERNATIVE). Codex T1 verdict at `.claude/state/codex_consult_w134_f27a_openai_agents_python_OUT.txt` STUDY-PILOT-PATTERN-EXTRACT conf=0.89.
docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:22:    5. **ECOSYSTEM-IMPORT** — core primitive GENUINELY-NEW at the surface level but imports parallel ecosystem at the dependency level. Disposition: **EVALUATE ecosystem cost vs core primitive value** (often CITE-PATTERN-ONLY when ecosystem footprint disproportionate). Example: Wave 134 Fire 27-B langgraph (Pregel BSP graph execution is novel BUT requires `langchain-core>=1.4.0a2` + 6+ langgraph-* sub-package import + LangSmith proprietary recommended). Pattern B HNF disposition at `.claude/state/codex_consult_w134_f27b_langgraph_OUT.txt`.
docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:24:    **Cite class for this 5-class lattice itself**: `constituents=[TIER-3-LOCAL-OPERATOR-DERIVED @ Wave 134 Fire 27-A + 27-B + 27-C codex T1 verdicts, TIER-2 @ existing cardinal-rule-12 scaffolding, TIER-2 @ `citation-discipline.md` rule #8 source-class reduction lattice precedent, TIER-1-DIRECT @ Anthropic + OpenAI + LangChain TIER-1 maintainer evidence]; effective_tier=TIER-3-LOCAL-COMPOSITION` per `citation-discipline.md` rule #8 MIN_PRECEDENCE.
docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:29:    - **PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT** vs **DUPLICATE-FUNCTIONALITY**: distinguished by whether both incumbents cover DIFFERENT scopes (PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT — both useful) or SAME scope (DUPLICATE — pick one)
docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:30:    - **PARTIAL-OVERLAP** vs **PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT**: distinguished by whether the DIFFERENT MECHANISMS suggest parallel co-existence (PROVIDER-COMPLEMENT) or competing-implementations (PARTIAL-OVERLAP requires case-by-case)
docs\sota-architecture-audit\fire-27d-cr12-5class-lattice-codification\01-proposed-claude-md-edit-draft.md:31:    - **ECOSYSTEM-IMPORT** is the OPERATIONAL escape valve when a candidate's core primitive is novel but ecosystem footprint creates duplicate-frameworks concern

Role-disambiguation: Beck=origin / Jeffries=verbatim author of canonical sentence / Fowler=canonical attribution source.
34:
35:Three non-negotiable shipping principles.
36:
37:## Keep It Simple (KISS)
38:
39:Prefer the simplest solution that actually works. Optimize for clarity, not cleverness. No premature optimization.
40:
41:## Don't Repeat Yourself (DRY)
42:
43:Extract repeated logic only when repetition is *real*, not speculative. Three similar lines is better than a premature abstraction (per root `CLAUDE.md` hard rule).
44:
45:## You Aren't Gonna Need It (YAGNI)
46:
47:Do not build features, flags, or abstractions before they are needed. No "future-proofing" shims, no backwards-compat layers for unreleased APIs.
48:
49:## Why
50:
51:Our harness has 10 agents (per `CLAUDE.md` D2 polish [VERIFIED 2026-04-27]) + 17 rules (per `CLAUDE.md` D1 polish [VERIFIED 2026-04-27]) + a growing `.claude/skills/` registry + `.claude/hooks/scripts/` infrastructure. Every premature abstraction is a landmine for the next wave of line-by-line audits. PARENT-ATTRIBUTION evidence ladder: cycles 112-116 caught 5 drift classes from old speculative scaffolds; cycle-72 refuted a hyperparameter (`λ_seed=0.3`) that existed only as a speculative knob — 0 consumers, 0 producers (full audit trail at parent `Z:/claude/rules/kiss-dry-yagni.md`).
52:
53:The root CLAUDE.md mandates: "Every changed line MUST trace to the user's request. No drive-by improvements." KISS/DRY/YAGNI is the hands-on instantiation of that mandate, and the operational form of Karpathy P2 (Simplicity First) per `karpathy-adapted.md` §2.
54:
55:## How to apply
56:
57:- Before extracting a helper: grep for the duplication. If <3 call sites, inline it.
58:- Before adding a config flag: check if anything reads it today. 0 consumers = delete the flag (PARENT-ATTRIBUTION per parent `feedback_dead_sentinel_silent_gate.md` — generic pattern; sss-local port not required, rule body fully captures lesson).
59:- Before a new abstraction layer: write the concrete path first, refactor only when a second caller actually arrives.
60:- Before a "nice to have" feature in a bug-fix PR: split it out. Bug fixes don't need surrounding cleanup.
61:- Post-change audit: run `grep -r "<new_symbol>"` — if only the definition site matches, you just wrote dead code.
62:
63:## Related rules
64:
65:- `karpathy-adapted.md` §2 — Karpathy P2 Simplicity First; this rule is the operational instantiation
66:- `canonical.md` Must Never #9 — cardinal hard-rule statement; this file ships the enforceable body
67:- `citation-discipline.md` — sister cardinal-rule body (cite-format contract); both are foundational discipline files
68:- `port-note-discipline.md` — when porting, do NOT speculatively add features beyond what parent had (YAGNI applied to the port itself)
69:- `evidence-policy.md` Stuck Detection — "Do not invent APIs" is YAGNI applied to API design

37:8. **Composed-claims discipline + mechanical source-class reduction lattice** — *(Wave 17 fire-31 v1 codification per codex T1 fire-28 conf=0.87; UPGRADED at fire-36 per codex T1 fire-33 NEEDS-REVISION on T2 b8fa7dd1 finding "weakest-source rule not computable" conf=0.72)* — When a single normative claim cites MULTIPLE source classes, the cite MUST declare:
38:   - `constituents=[<class1@cite1>, <class2@cite2>, ...]` — explicit list of each constituent primitive at file:line + SHA OR official-docs URL
39:   - `effective_tier=<class>` — the EFFECTIVE class of the composed claim, computed by the reduction lattice below
40:
41:   **Source-class precedence/order (lower wins; weakest dominates)**:
42:   1. `UNKNOWN` (no cite at all) — always disqualifying; reject claim until cited
43:   2. `TIER-3-LOCAL-COMPOSITION` (any local glue / sss-novel composition over TIER-1/TIER-2 substrates)
44:   3. `TIER-3-LOCAL-OPERATOR-DERIVED` (sss dogfood, codex verdicts, incidents, operator decisions)
45:   4. `TIER-3-LOCAL-CONFIG` (sss live config or script wiring)
46:   5. `TIER-2` (user-curated/sibling docs, NOT upstream authority)
47:   6. `TIER-1-COMPOSED` (ALL constituents TIER-1 with disclosed local glue) — still TIER-3-LOCAL-COMPOSITION as effective tier
48:   7. `TIER-1-DIRECT` (upstream verbatim file:line + SHA OR official-docs URL with anchor)
49:
50:   **Reduction rule (mechanical)**: `effective_tier = MIN_PRECEDENCE(constituents)`. Concretely: if ANY constituent contains "TIER-3-LOCAL-*" OR the composition glue itself is local-codified (e.g., sss-novel composition pattern), the effective tier is `TIER-3-LOCAL-COMPOSITION` regardless of how many TIER-1 primitives are cited. EXCEPTION: if the composed claim is ONLY about an upstream primitive's EXISTENCE (e.g., "asyncRewake field exists" cited verbatim from Anthropic docs), it remains `TIER-1-DIRECT` because there's no local composition glue.
51:
52:   **Anti-promotion rule**: composition CANNOT promote a TIER-2/TIER-3 component into TIER-1. The cite class of the COMPOSED claim is determined by the MIN_PRECEDENCE constituent OR by the composition-glue class, whichever is weaker.
53:
54:   **Exemplar (computable)**: `.claude/rules/cross-model-consensus.md §Normative Authority Map` row "T1-T7 touchpoint lifecycle":

ccbp-claude-mcp-full\\n## Configuration\\r\\n\\r\\nMCP servers are configured in `.mcp.json` at the project root (project-scoped) or in `~/.claude.json` (user-scoped).\\r\\n\\r\\n### Server Types\\r\\n\\r\\n| Type | Transport | Example |\\r\\n|------|-----------|---------|\\r\\n| **stdio** | Spawns a local process | `npx`, `python`, binary |\\r\\n| **http** | Connects to a remote URL | HTTP/SSE endpoint |\\r\\n\\r\\n### Example `.mcp.json`\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\r\\n  \\\"mcpServers\\\": {\\r\\n    \\\"context7\\\": {\\r\\n      \\\"command\\\": \\\"npx\\\",\\r\\n      \\\"args\\\": [\\\"-y\\\", \\\"@upstash/context7-mcp\\\"]\\r\\n    },\\r\\n    \\\"playwright\\\": {\\r\\n      \\\"command\\\": \\\"npx\\\",\\r\\n      \\\"args\\\": [\\\"-y\\\", \\\"@playwright/mcp\\\"]\\r\\n    },\\r\\n    \\\"deepwiki\\\": {\\r\\n      \\\"command\\\": \\\"npx\\\",\\r\\n      \\\"args\\\": [\\\"-y\\\", \\\"deepwiki-mcp\\\"]\\r\\n    },\\r\\n    \\\"remote-api\\\": {\\r\\n      \\\"type\\\": \\\"http\\\",\\r\\n      \\\"url\\\": \\\"https://mcp.example.com/mcp\\\"\\r\\n    }\\r\\n  }\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nUse environment variable expansion for secrets instead of committing API keys in `.mcp.json`:\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\r\\n  \\\"mcpServers\\\": {\\r\\n    \\\"remote-api\\\": {\\r\\n      \\\"type\\\": \\\"http\\\",\\r\\n      \\\"url\\\": \\\"https://mcp.example.com/mcp?token=${MCP_API_TOKEN}\\\"\\r\\n    }\\r\\n  }\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n### Settings for MCP Servers\\r\\n\\r\\nThese settings in `.claude/settings.json` control MCP server approval:\\r\\n\\r\\n| Key | Type | Description |\\r\\n|-----|------|-------------|\\r\\n| `enableAllProjectMcpServers` | boolean | Auto-approve all `.mcp.json` servers without prompting |\\r\\n| `enabledMcpjsonServers` | array | Allowlist of specific server names to auto-approve |\\r\\n| `disabledMcpjsonServers` | array | Blocklist of specific server names to reject |\\r\\n\\r\\n### Permission Rules for MCP Tools\\r\\n\\r\\nMCP tools follow the `mcp__<server>__<tool>` naming convention in permission rules:\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\r\\n  \\\"permissions\\\": {\\r\\n    \\\"allow\\\": [\\r\\n      \\\"mcp__*\\\",\\r\\n      \\\"mcp__context7__*\\\",\\r\\n      \\\"mcp__playwright__browser_snapshot\\\"\\r\\n    ],\\r\\n    \\\"deny\\\": [\\r\\n      \\\"mcp__dangerous-server__*\\\"\\r\\n    ]\\r\\n  }\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\n\\n### eee-mcp-json (2)\\n{\\n  \\\"_comment\\\": \\\"Wave 75 2026-05-08 — Tier-2A HTTP MCPs (github + context7 + ccbp-claude-mcp-full\\n## Configuration\\r\\n\\r\\nMCP servers are configured in `.mcp.json` at the project root (project-scoped) or in `~/.claude.json` (user-scoped).\\r\\n\\r\\n### Server Types\\r\\n\\r\\n| Type | Transport | Example |\\r\\n|------|-----------|---------|\\r\\n| **stdio** | Spawns a local process | `npx`, `python`, binary |\\r\\n| **http** | Connects to a remote URL | HTTP/SSE endpoint |\\r\\n\\r\\n### Example `.mcp.json`\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\r\\n  \\\"mcpServers\\\": {\\r\\n    \\\"context7\\\": {\\r\\n      \\\"command\\\": \\\"npx\\\",\\r\\n      \\\"args\\\": [\\\"-y\\\", \\\"@upstash/context7-mcp\\\"]\\r\\n    },\\r\\n    \\\"playwright\\\": {\\r\\n      \\\"command\\\": \\\"npx\\\",\\r\\n      \\\"args\\\": [\\\"-y\\\", \\\"@playwright/mcp\\\"]\\r\\n    },\\r\\n    \\\"deepwiki\\\": {\\r\\n      \\\"command\\\": \\\"npx\\\",\\r\\n      \\\"args\\\": [\\\"-y\\\", \\\"deepwiki-mcp\\\"]\\r\\n    },\\r\\n    \\\"remote-api\\\": {\\r\\n      \\\"type\\\": \\\"http\\\",\\r\\n      \\\"url\\\": \\\"https://mcp.example.com/mcp\\\"\\r\\n    }\\r\\n  }\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\nUse environment variable expansion for secrets instead of committing API keys in `.mcp.json`:\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\r\\n  \\\"mcpServers\\\": {\\r\\n    \\\"remote-api\\\": {\\r\\n      \\\"type\\\": \\\"http\\\",\\r\\n      \\\"url\\\": \\\"https://mcp.example.com/mcp?token=${MCP_API_TOKEN}\\\"\\r\\n    }\\r\\n  }\\r\\n}\\r\\n```\\r\\n\\r\\n### Settings for MCP Servers\\r\\n\\r\\nThese settings in `.claude/settings.json` control MCP server approval:\\r\\n\\r\\n| Key | Type | Description |\\r\\n|-----|------|-------------|\\r\\n| `enableAllProjectMcpServers` | boolean | Auto-approve all `.mcp.json` servers without prompting |\\r\\n| `enabledMcpjsonServers` | array | Allowlist of specific server names to auto-approve |\\r\\n| `disabledMcpjsonServers` | array | Blocklist of specific server names to reject |\\r\\n\\r\\n### Permission Rules for MCP Tools\\r\\n\\r\\nMCP tools follow the `mcp__<server>__<tool>` naming convention in permission rules:\\r\\n\\r\\n```json\\r\\n{\\r\\n  \\\"permissions\\\": {\\r\\n    \\\"allow\\\": [\\r\\n      \\\"mcp__*\\\",\\r\\n      \\\"mcp__context7__*\\\",\\r\\n      \\\"mcp__playwright__browser_snapshot\\\"\\r\\n    ],\\r\\n    \\\"deny\\\":
